$doc: MQ Research Gate — architecture & monetization atlas. Machine-readable source of truth for AI chats. Human view: docs/atlas.html. Feedback log: docs/feedback.json.

app.name: MQ Research Gate
app.oneLiner: A detective's study for the Qur'an: meaning is earned from within the text (the organic Qur'anic methodology). Notice a word, open a case on its root family, gather every place the Book uses it, form a hypothesis, then weigh the classical dictionaries.
app.stack: React + Vite + TypeScript SPA (app/), run on the reader's machine (desktop, or npm start). The research server (remote/, Hono + Postgres + Better Auth) holds the Qur'an corpus, every account's private research, and the community. MCP server (mcp/) lets an AI study and propose, as its user. The local server (server/) remains for local tools, tests and bringing an old research.db in. Electron desktop wrapper (electron/).

principle.core: Features are ROLE-based (what you may do); resources are PLAN-based (what you may read). Your research is private to your account; only what you publish is shared, only once approved, and only with the audience it names.
principle.constraint: You can only enforceably charge for what the server holds.
principle.consequence: Everything lives on the research server: the corpus, each account's research (its own Postgres schema), the community. The app and the MCP read and write it as the signed-in user.

components.name: App
components.runtime: React 18 + Vite SPA (on the reader's machine)
components.role: Reads the corpus (${REMOTE_URL}/corpus) and reads/writes the reader's research (${REMOTE_URL}/research) with the session cookie; the community likewise. Settings → Your research: download a copy, import a research.db, bring this computer's old research in. Maintainers get an Admin tab.

components.name: Local server
components.role: No longer where research lives. Serves the same corpus and research routes over local files — for tests, local tools, and GET /api/v1/research/file, which the app uploads to bring an old research.db into the account.

components.name: MCP
components.role: An AI studies the corpus and proposes into the reader's research, AS the reader (REMOTE_TOKEN). The server enforces the AI boundary on every token write. MQ_CORPUS=local / MQ_RESEARCH=local use local files instead.

components.name: Research server
components.role: Auth (cookie or API token), the role ladder, plan tiers, resource rules, the corpus (/corpus), each account's research (/research, one schema per account), the community with audiences, Admin endpoints. Deployed with Docker + Caddy (DEPLOY.md).

components.name: Desktop
components.role: Wraps the built SPA + local server in a desktop window.

corpus (Postgres schema `corpus`).holds: Qur'an text in four scripts, per-word morphology (root/lemma/form), roots, ~10 classical lexicons, translations, search indexes. Copied from quran.db and verified exact.
corpus (Postgres schema `corpus`).load: npm run corpus:migrate (-- --verify to re-verify only). remote/src/corpus/{schema,load,verify}.ts. 294,804 rows, 143.5 MB, 18 s.
corpus (Postgres schema `corpus`).collation: every text column COLLATE "C" (= SQLite BINARY) so Arabic sorts identically.
corpus (Postgres schema `corpus`).parity: npm run corpus:parity — the SAME corpus routes over each driver, compared over HTTP. Full sweep 2026-09-26: 77,439 requests (every chapter, verse, root, root pair, word, search) — all identical. --quick samples ~3k.

quran.db.holds: The same corpus in SQLite. Now the SOURCE for corpus:migrate, the local driver (MQ_CORPUS=local, tests, offline MCP) and the parity reference. The app no longer reads it.

research.db.location: the reader's machine — before research moved to the account
research.db.holds: The same tables. Now: what 'Bring it into my account' uploads (the file itself is never changed), the local driver for tests and MQ_RESEARCH=local, and the format of 'Download a copy'.
research.db.ownership: A one-row owner table (name, email, uuidv5-of-email) — the same uuid the account's research carries, so imported work stays theirs.

research (Postgres, one schema per accou.access: private to its account; read-write by that account (and its AI, within the boundary)
research (Postgres, one schema per accou.location: the research server — schema research_<account id>
research (Postgres, one schema per accou.holds: cases + board layout, form_research + form_revisions, trails, notes, word_indications (+ refinements), user_root_meanings, motifs, comparisons, settings, and the outbox of what was published.
research (Postgres, one schema per accou.isolation: Every request runs in one transaction with SET LOCAL search_path to the signed-in account's schema — taken only from the authenticated principal. No route reads another person's research; staff included.
research (Postgres, one schema per accou.shape: Derived from the research.db DDL itself (INTEGER→BIGINT, TEXT→TEXT COLLATE "C"), so a file and a schema can't drift. Proven: 78 scripted research calls answer identically over both (research-cloud.test.ts).
research (Postgres, one schema per accou.transfer: POST /research/import merges a research.db in (adds, never overwrites or deletes; twice adds nothing); GET /research/export downloads a complete research.db.

accessModel.rule: Features are role-based; resources are plan-based. Everything fails closed.

roles.ladder: DATA: table role_levels (name, rank, label, fixed). Seeded reader 0 · student 10 · researcher 20 · scholar 30 · moderator 80 · maintainer 100. reader, moderator and maintainer are FIXED (the staff powers hang on them); learner rungs sit between (rank 1–79) and are the maintainer's to add, rename, re-rank or remove.
roles.meaning: A person's standing — what they may DO. A principal carries its role's rank (loaded at sign-in), so guards compare ranks; unknown roles rank below everyone.

features.publish (submit / propose): feature_access 'publish' — researcher by default, the maintainer's choice

roles.file: remote/src/roles.ts (guards, no DB), remote/src/role-ladder.ts (ladder, requireFeature, audiences)

plans.ladder: DATA: table plan_tiers (name, rank, label). Seeded free (0) < pro (100); a maintainer adds e.g. student 50, scholar 200 in the Admin tab. free is always rank 0.
plans.meaning: What you may READ. A higher rank unlocks everything a lower one does; a lapsed plan (users.plan_expires_at past) counts as free.

resources.table: resource_access (kind, key, min_plan). min_plan = a tier, 'free' (= any signed-in account), or NULL (= public, no sign-in).

whole.community: key '*' — community readings, claims, dissents, divergences, pull (default pro)

perItem.translation: key = resource id; below its tier the translation is LEFT OUT of results
perItem.lexicon: key = source (lanes_lexicon, lisan_ul_arab, …); below its tier the entries are left out of a root page

resources.noRule: An item with no rule needs only what the corpus needs.
resources.refusal: requireResource(kind) → 401 {detail} if a sign-in is needed, 402 {detail, resource, plan} if a higher plan is.

accessModel.edit: In the app: Admin → Roles (the ladder, 'What each role may do'), Plan tiers, Who can read, Translations, Dictionaries, People. Scripted: npm run access / set-plan.
accessModel.billing: Not wired yet. A maintainer grants plans in the Admin tab (or set-plan / POST /plan). That is the single seam a payment provider slots into.

audiences.rule: Every published result (claim version, submission) carries an audience: at least a role AND at least a plan (either may be empty). The author proposes it; the reviewer confirms or changes it when approving/establishing. Nothing is visible before approval except to its author and staff.
audiences.enforcement: Every community read — claims, the group's reading, dissents, readings/chips, divergences and their count, the pull — filters by the viewer's role rank and plan. Authors always see their own; staff (moderator+) see everything, since they review it. The community resource rule (plan) still applies to all of it.
audiences.file: remote/src/role-ladder.ts makeAudienceCheck; claims.ts / pull.ts take a CanSee

auth.cookie: Better Auth session cookie — the app (credentials: 'include').
auth.apiTokens: Personal API tokens (mqrg_…, stored as SHA-256; secret shown once) for headless clients — the MCP. Sent as `Authorization: Bearer`. Made in the app: Account → Connect an AI assistant (it prints a ready MCP config). remote/src/api-tokens.ts, session.ts. A token acts exactly as its user, so the MCP reads what that user's plan allows.

corpusCode.oneCodebase: server/src/corpus-db.ts defines CorpusDb {query, one, scalar} (async). Every corpus service (content, roots, linkages, wazn, expressions, echoes, spellings, freetext, similarity, morphology) is written once against it.
corpusCode.services: createCorpusServices(db) in server/src/corpus-services.ts; warmCorpus builds the memoised indexes (the cloud warms them at startup).
corpusCode.routes: server/src/routes/{content,roots,similarity,echoes,corpus}.ts take (services, entitlements). The local server mounts them at /api/v1; the cloud mounts the identical builders at /corpus (remote/src/corpus/serve.ts) with the plan filters as entitlements.
portableSql: a total ORDER BY wherever order is visible
DISTINCT → GROUP BY … ORDER BY MIN(id)
nullable sort keys NULLS FIRST (ASC) / NULLS LAST (DESC)
Postgres int8 counts normalised to numbers

clients.app: app/src/api/client.ts: CORPUS = ${REMOTE_URL}/corpus. A refused read announces itself (CORPUS_ACCESS_EVENT) and CorpusAccessBanner says why once, at the top: offline / sign in / needs the X plan — and 'Your access has changed, reload' after a sign-in or plan grant.
clients.mcp: mcp/src/corpus-client.ts: CorpusReads with remoteReads (HTTP, default) and localReads (MQ_CORPUS=local). 401 → 'create a token', 402 → 'needs the X plan', unreachable → 'set REMOTE_URL or MQ_CORPUS=local'. server/test/mcp-remote-corpus.test.ts runs every corpus tool on both paths: byte-identical.

mcpEnv.QF_RESEARCH_DB: research.db path (default: the repo's; the app's current file is used)

the whole corpus API — same paths/params/JSON as the local /api/v1 (verses, chapters, words, roots, linkages, echoes, similar, spellings, wazn, phrase/expression/free-text search); translations + lexicons filtered by tier
the invite code is the credential

decisions.decision: Research lives on the research server, private to each account, in its own Postgres schema.
decisions.why: The maintainer's call, 2026-09-27. It follows the reader across devices and is backed up centrally; privacy by construction (schema-per-account, search_path from the principal only). Cost: studying needs the server; the operator can technically read the database, like any hosted app.

decisions.decision: student and scholar are ROLES (standing), not plan tiers; plans stay about paying.
decisions.why: The maintainer's call. A published result can then say 'scholar role or higher AND pro plan'.

decisions.decision: The publisher proposes a result's audience; the reviewer confirms or changes it at approval.
decisions.why: The maintainer's call. The author knows who it's for; the reviewer is accountable for what the community sees.

decisions.decision: Every feature is role-based; every resource is plan-based.
decisions.why: Maintainer's call, 2026-09-26: 'it will be easier.' One question per gate: may you DO this (role), may you READ this (plan).

decisions.decision: The corpus lives in Postgres and the cloud serves it; the app and MCP read it from /corpus.
decisions.why: The maintainer's call. Makes the corpus a gateable resource. Cost: reading needs the research server (the banner says so; MQ_CORPUS=local keeps the MCP working offline).

decisions.decision: One corpus code path over a driver interface, not a Postgres twin.
decisions.why: A twin drifts. With one codebase, parity is a property of SQL portability, proven by comparing the same routes over both drivers.

decisions.decision: Administration is an Admin tab for maintainers, not only a CLI.
decisions.why: Maintainer's request. The CLI stays for scripting.

decisions.decision: The MCP authenticates with a personal API token and reads as its user.
decisions.why: A headless process can't hold a browser session; a revocable token keeps the plan gate honest for the AI too.

decisions.decision: A translation or lexicon above the caller's tier is left out, not refused.
decisions.why: One verse carries many translations; refusing the whole page for one locked item would be wrong.

decisions.decision: Community data is read live from the remote, never mirrored into research.db.
decisions.why: Mirroring puts it on the reader's disk, which makes it un-gateable.

decisions.decision: Plan is a separate axis from role.
decisions.why: A moderator on free can moderate; a paying reader isn't a researcher. A tier named 'admin' is only what's paid for.

decisions.decision: The last maintainer can't be demoted.
decisions.why: It would lock everyone out of administering the community.

glossary.feature: Something you DO (publish, review, establish, administer). Gated by role.
glossary.resource: Something you READ (the corpus, the community, a translation, a dictionary). Gated by plan.
glossary.tier: A rung on the plan ladder (plan_tiers). Higher rank unlocks more.
glossary.min_plan: A resource's requirement: a tier, 'free' (signed in), or NULL (public).
glossary.API token: mqrg_… — a revocable credential that acts as its user; how the MCP signs in.
glossary.locally established: A form meaning YOU established, in your own research.db.
glossary.globally established: The reading moderators accepted as the group's; lives on the cloud.
glossary.dissent: A recorded disagreement with a globally established reading, preserved not resolved.
glossary.divergence (⚖): A form you established whose meaning differs from the group's. Computed live on the remote.
glossary.audience: Who may see a published result: at least a role and at least a plan. Proposed by the author, confirmed by the reviewer.
glossary.role ladder: reader < student < researcher < scholar < moderator < maintainer — data the maintainer edits; the three fixed rungs carry the staff powers.

notice: The maintainer account (mansoor@wimetrix.com) is maintainer · free, and the corpus + community rules are pro — so the app will say reading needs the pro plan. Admin → People → Change → Pro, or Admin → Who can read. Their existing research is still in the local research.db: Settings → Your research → 'Bring it into my account' moves a copy into the account (the file stays as it is).

Submissions have an audience but no review UI in the app yet (claims do).

deployment.shape: One Linux VPS, docker compose (deploy/): Postgres 16 + the research server (remote/Dockerfile) + Caddy (automatic HTTPS). Only 80/443 exposed.
deployment.container: entrypoint: serve (config check → migrations → server) | corpus-migrate | corpus-parity | bootstrap | set-password | set-plan | access | smoke
deployment.safety: NODE_ENV=production refuses to start without a real AUTH_SECRET, DATABASE_URL, an https REMOTE_BASE_URL, or with SMTP chosen but unset (config.ts deployProblems).
deployment.cookies: Over HTTPS the session cookie is SameSite=None; Secure — the app runs on the reader's localhost, a different site from the server.
deployment.email: SMTP (nodemailer, src/mailer.ts): password reset (app: Account → Email me a reset link → the server's /reset-password page) and magic links. console transport prints them.
deployment.backups: deploy/backup.sh — nightly pg_dump, 14 days; copy off the machine.
deployment.appBuild: VITE_REMOTE_URL=https://<domain> at build time (desktop:dist or npm start).
